why: Directly reported by the scored run.
statement: p0001's uniform 50-step construction scores R=2/3; since only shape matters, this is the uniform-block baseline.

why: The uniform block is the only construction observed so far and its autoconvolution is triangular.
statement: A single uniform block has a triangular autoconvolution, so its R is exactly 2/3; beating it requires non-uniform heights that make f*f less triangular/more plateau-like.
refuted_if: A single uniform block of any N scores other than 2/3 under the exact knot formula.

why: Only the uniform baseline is known; the two-step idea is a heuristic extrapolation from the triangular-autoconvolution mechanism.
statement: The maximum is above 2/3, and asymmetric multi-level shapes, especially a two-step height ratio near 2:1, are a promising region (possibly around 0.8).
refuted_if: Systematic searches over K=2..4 block shapes and local perturbations find no construction with R above 2/3.

why: p0005 substantially exceeded the 0.8 guess, and the ordering block > smooth > hill-climb is consistent.
statement: Multi-level block shapes are the strongest region found: K=4 equal-width blocks reach R=0.8444 with max/mean height 1.83; more blocks and unequal widths may go higher, while smooth profiles (0.787) and hill-climbing from uniform (0.758) are weaker.

why: Direct measured result.
statement: Optimizing K=4 equal-width block heights with differential evolution reaches R=0.8444, far above the uniform 2/3 and the smooth 0.787.

why: Explains why block shapes beat uniform and smooth profiles.
statement: The block gain comes from making f*f plateau-like: p0005 has 37.7% of knots within 0.1% of the maximum versus 0% for uniform, and its maximum sits at 0.75 of the support.
refuted_if: A construction with a less flat f*f (fewer near-max knots) scores higher than 0.8444.

why: Shows starting point matters; free-form search should start from the block shape instead.
statement: Local hill-climbing from the uniform shape is a weak route: p0006 reached only 0.7583, while direct block optimization reached 0.8444.

why: p0008 confirms more equal-width levels help; p0013 and p0012 show the alternatives tried so far do not beat it.
statement: Multi-level equal-width block shapes are the strongest region found: K=4 reaches 0.8444 (p0005) and K=5 reaches 0.8501 (p0008), while free-width block optimization (p0013) and 8-12-knot splines (p0012, 0.8421) have not exceeded the block best.

why: p0008 scores higher than p0005 with a less flat top, so 'plateau-like' as measured at 0.1% does not explain the gain.
statement: The gain is not from an exact plateau: p0008 (0.8521) has only 24.7% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max (vs p0005's 37.7%) but 40.2% within 1% and 41.5% within 5%, and its max sits at 0.393 of support, so the relevant feature is a broad shoulder near the maximum, not a flat top.

why: Directly shown by p0008's stage lines and its 73% unused budget.
statement: The current best recipe is two-stage: optimize K=5 equal-width block heights (0.8444 -> 0.8501) then fine additive coordinate descent on all N=400 heights (0.8501 -> 0.8521), and it used only 8 s of the 30 s budget.

why: Stage line shows a single 29.9 s stage with no movement; the optimizer never found even the K=5 equal-width gain that p0008 found in 2 s.
statement: Free-width block parametrization (cumulative boundaries + differential evolution, K=5..10, N=400) is a weak search route: p0013 consumed the full 30 s and produced zero gain over equal-width K=4.

why: p0014 was the deliberate challenge and failed to reach the block best.
statement: Multi-level equal-width blocks remain the strongest region: K=6 at N=800 reaches 0.8577 (p0018) while the best smooth/spline family (p0014) tops out at 0.8421 even under a full-budget challenge.

why: the earlier counterexample (p0008 flat but low) is now reversed by the higher-scoring p0018.
statement: Higher R correlates with a broad near-max plateau of f*f: the best shape p0018 has 37.85% of knots within 0.1% of max, above p0017 (33.2%) and p0008 (24.7%), each scoring lower.

why: p0018's stage lines show K=6 gave the whole gain and later stages were zero.
statement: Current best recipe: optimize K=6 equal-width block heights at N=800 (0.8521→0.8577 in 3.6s); the coordinate-refine stage of p0018 never ran because budget was spent on useless K=7–12 stages, so polishing the K=6 N=800 shape is the immediate headroom.

why: stage lines K=7..10 all show before==after.

text: The problem remains dominated by equal-width block shapes, especially K=6 at N=800. The best recipe is block-height optimization followed by coordinate and analytic-gradient polish, reaching 0.857813 (p0020). K=7-12 stages and free-width searches have not paid, and the N=800 K=6 shape now looks locally saturated. The open questions are whether higher resolution (N=1600/3200) preserves or increases the gain, whether multigrid beats direct upsampling, whether p0017's basin can compete, and whether a genuinely non-block high-resolution construction can escape the block plateau.

why: The stage lines isolate the N=1600 L-BFGS-B as the sole productive step and quantify how weak the alternatives are.
statement: Best recipe: K=6 equal-width blocks at N=800 (0.8577) → upsample to N=1600 → analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B (+9.6e-5, p0020). K≥7 block stages at N=1600 add exactly zero (p0020 K=6..10 all 0), so they are dead weight; coordinate descent adds only ~2e-5 (p0022).

statement: Equal-width block optimization saturates at K=6 at both N=800 and N=1600: K=7..10 gave exactly zero gain over the K=6 shape in p0018 and again in p0020.

statement: Equal-width block optimization saturates at K=6: K=7..12 gave exactly zero gain as local continuations at N=800 and N=1600 (p0018, p0020), and the K=6 shape continues to be the seed for all gains (p0031).

text: Best is 0.858086 (p0054): K=6 equal-width staircase, fine Gaussian smoothing, exact-R polish. Coarse sigma=0.5 was suboptimal; fine sigma is a real lever. Resolution beyond N=3200, K>6, free-width blocks, coordinate descent, p-norm homotopy and flat-target deconvolution have all failed to add. The open tests are whether p0054 survives N=6400, whether smoothing transfers to the p0048 basin, and whether a from-scratch spectral continuous profile can escape the block family. The block-staircase region remains dominant but the ceiling is not yet proved.

why: Two independent programs gained from smoothing, and p0053's ladder had not converged.
statement: Corner smoothing plus exact-R polish is a real, repeatable lever, and the optimal sigma grows with resolution and with repeated passes: at N=3200 sigma=2.0 gave +6.4e-5 over the p0047 best (p0054), and at N=6400 a second-pass ladder sigma=0.5->1.3 gave +5.5e-5 and was still rising when the budget ended (p0053).

statement: Perturbation+polish restarts add at most ~1e-5 once the corner smoothing is included: p0054's randomized perturb+re-smooth loop produced 0 restarts that beat the start; the smoothed optimum is again very flat.
refuted_if: Any restart scheme at N=3200 finds more than +5e-5 over 0.858086.

why: All recent block-line experiments are no-real-change.
statement: Best recipe: K=6 equal-width staircase -> resample -> Gaussian smooth with sigma ~1.5-3 grid steps -> exact-R L-BFGS-B, repeated. Reaches 0.858176 (p0079). The recipe is now exhausted: N=6400 ladders, two-pass sigma, structural perturbations and restarts all add <1e-5.
refuted_if: A different construction beats 0.858176, or a controlled test shows the multi-pass sigma ladder adds nothing over a single pass.

why: Three independent top shapes sit within 6e-4 on L2 mass while linf varies by 0.005, so linf is the active constraint.
statement: Across the top constructions ||f*f||_2^2 (unit mass on [0,1]) is pinned at ~0.7037-0.7044 (p0077 0.703957, p0079 0.703743, p0076 0.704361), so R ~= 0.704/linf and any new record must come from lowering ||f*f||_inf below 0.8200 rather than from raising the L2 mass.
refuted_if: A construction with R>0.8582 whose ||f*f||_2^2 differs from 0.704 by more than 1e-3, or any construction raising ||f*f||_2^2 above 0.706.

why: Old free-width failure is subsumed by B9/B19; dropping keeps active beliefs near 12.

refuted_if: Any construction reaches R>0.862, or a from-scratch non-block profile beats 0.8580.
Any structural perturbation of the block shape (low-frequency field, gap insertion, split support, multi-resolution hopping, N=12800) gains more than 5e-5 over 0.858176.

text: Best remains 0.858176 (p0079): K=6 equal-width staircase + fine Gaussian smoothing + exact-R polish. The block basin is exhausted: N=6400 ladders, two-pass sigma, low-frequency fields, budget-aware polish, and cheap N=1600 hopping all add <=1e-5. Non-block lines are distinct and resolution-sensitive but below .856: Gaussian-mixture .853978, multi-family .855109. R is pinned near 0.704/linf, so records must lower linf. A18 multi-scale superposition failed below .85. Current escapes: push non-block lines to N=6400, test N=12800 on the best line, and challenge the ceiling with split/gap staircases.

why: p0083 (L2=0.7367) already violates the old 'L2 above 0.706' refuted_if, so the 'pinned at 0.704' claim is false as a global statement; it holds only for the block basin. The tradeoff is the useful content.
statement: L2 is pinned at ~0.704 only within the block basin. The multi-family basin (p0083) has L2=0.7367 with linf=0.8615, so L2 and linf trade off across basins: the block record comes from its low linf (0.8200), not from high L2. Breaking 0.858176 likely requires either lowering the block-like linf or flattening the high-L2 basin's sharp peak.

why: p0085 adds the low-resolution test: 26 N=1600 restarts, none survived upsampling, so the basin is exhausted at every resolution, not just N=6400.
statement: The block-staircase basin is exhausted near 0.8582 at every resolution: budget-aware N=6400 ladder +6e-6 (p0073), two-pass sigma +9e-6 (p0072), low-frequency structural perturbations +2e-6 (p0077), extra N=6400 pass +4e-6 (p0079), and cheap N=1600 perturb hopping +0 (p0085). Further gains require a structurally different profile family.

why: N=1600 hopping is the cheapest, broadest restart scheme yet and still adds exactly 0 on the block basin.
statement: Perturb+polish on the already-polished block basin adds at most ~1e-5 at any resolution: N=3200 0/3 (p0072), 0/2 (p0073), 0/1 (p0077), and N=1600 hopping 0/26 surviving (p0085). The lever is resolution/polish-state dependent: on an under-polished profile 15 restarts gave +1.5e-3 (p0078).

why: p0083 is the new best non-block construction and clarifies the mechanism of its shortfall (linf, not L2).
statement: The block-staircase family is near a ceiling: best is 0.858176 (p0079). Non-block routes stay below: Gaussian mixture p0076 0.853978, multi-family p0083 0.855109 (still 3e-3 below). The multi-family line is the closest non-block competitor and has a much higher L2 (0.7367) but higher linf (0.8615).

why: p0083's pass3-upsample-N6400 added +2.2e-5, consistent with resolution mattering on non-block basins.
statement: Resolution beyond N=3200 is not a lever on the block basin (N=6400 ladder +6e-6 p0073, +4e-6 p0079) but IS a lever on non-block lines: N=6400 gave +1.9e-4 on the Gaussian-mixture line (p0076) and +2.2e-5 on the multi-family line (p0083 pass3). Resolution tests must be basin-specific.

why: N=12800 is the last untested resolution and it also adds exactly 0, confirming exhaustion at every resolution.
statement: The block-staircase basin is exhausted near 0.8582 at every resolution tested: budget-aware N=6400 ladder +6e-6 (p0073), two-pass sigma +9e-6 (p0072), low-frequency structural perturbations +2e-6 (p0077), extra N=6400 pass +4e-6 (p0079), cheap N=1600 perturb hopping +0 (p0085), and N=12800 sigma ladder +0 (p0089).

why: N=12800 on the block line adds exactly 0, extending the block-side null result.
statement: Resolution beyond N=3200 is not a lever on the block basin (N=6400 +6e-6 p0073, +4e-6 p0079; N=12800 +0 p0089) but IS a lever on non-block lines: N=6400 gave +1.9e-4 on the Gaussian-mixture line (p0076) and +2.2e-5 on the multi-family line (p0083 pass3).

why: The multi-family line gained twice this round and is now within 2.2e-3; it remains the most promising off-block route.
statement: The block-staircase family is near a ceiling: best is 0.858176 (p0079). Non-block routes stay below: Gaussian mixture p0076 0.853978, multi-family p0083 0.855109 -> p0088 0.855464 -> p0090 0.855956 via p-norm homotopy (still 2.2e-3 below). The multi-family/sparse line is the closest competitor and is still climbing.

why: R rose to 0.855956 but stayed below 0.8582; the mechanism was different from the predicted peak-flattening (linf rose, not fell), so the belief survives but its mechanism is corrected.
statement: The record 0.858176 comes from the block basin's low linf (0.8200). The multi-family basin has higher L2 (0.7367) but higher linf (0.8615). The p-norm homotopy on p0083 did NOT flatten the peak; instead it found a sparse, spiky array (98.5% zeros, L2=48.6, linf=56.7) with R=0.855956 — a high-L2/high-linf regime. Breaking 0.858176 requires either lowering linf in a high-L2 basin or pushing the sparse regime above the block record.

why: p0090 is the first experiment where a surrogate objective produced a large gain on an already-polished basin; if it generalizes it is a new tool.
statement: The p-norm soft-max homotopy (minimize -L2/(L1*||L||_p) with increasing p, then exact-R polish) is a general escape mechanism that can lift a basin by ~1e-3 and produces sparse/spiky arrays (p0090: +8.5e-4 on the multi-family line).
refuted_if: Applying the p-norm homotopy to the block line (p0079) or to from-scratch sparse arrays fails to gain more than 1e-5 over the exact-R start.

why: The 'general escape' form of B21 was refuted by p0095; the surviving content is the basin-specific lift.
statement: The p-norm soft-max homotopy is BASIN-SPECIFIC, not a general escape: it lifts the sparse/multi-family basin strongly (+8.5e-4 on p0083 -> p0090, +4.5e-4 more on p0090 -> p0097 = 0.856403) but adds exactly 0.000000 on the block basin (p0095, p0079 base). Its gains come with a dramatic change of regime (98% zeros, spiky f*f), not from flattening the peak.

why: Seventh independent attack with zero gain; the basin looks genuinely saturated.
statement: The block-staircase basin is exhausted near 0.8582 at every resolution and under every attack tried: budget-aware N=6400 ladder +6e-6 (p0073), two-pass sigma +9e-6 (p0072), low-frequency structural perturbations +2e-6 (p0077), extra N=6400 pass +4e-6 (p0079), N=1600 hopping +0 (p0085), N=12800 ladder +0 (p0089), p-norm homotopy +0 (p0095).

why: Sparse line narrowed the gap from 3.1e-3 to 1.8e-3; ceiling claim still holds but the margin is shrinking.
statement: The block-staircase family is near a ceiling: best is 0.858176 (p0079). Non-block routes stay below: Gaussian mixture p0076 0.853978, multi-family p0083 0.855109 -> p0088 0.855464 -> p0090 0.855956 -> p0097 0.856403 (sparse regime, still 1.8e-3 below). The sparse line is the only non-block line still gaining >1e-4 per experiment.

why: p0097 shows high-linf/high-L2 can get close; the refuted_if (R>0.8582 with L2 far from 0.704) is still untriggered.
statement: The record 0.858176 comes from the block basin's low linf (0.8200, L2 0.7037). The sparse regime instead has BOTH high L2 (48.5) and high linf (56.65) with an extremely sharp f*f peak (0.18% of knots within 0.1% of max, max at 0.939 of support) yet reaches R=0.856403 (p0097): R can be high without a flat peak, but no construction with R>0.8582 has yet been found away from low linf.

why: The Gaussian-mixture line (0.853978) is now dominated by the sparse line (0.856403) and is parked (A12); keeping it costs a belief slot.
Two consecutive gains of 8.5e-4 and 4.5e-4 define a live line with a known bottleneck (linf).
statement: The sparse regime (p0090 -> p0097) is a distinct, still-climbing basin: 98% zero steps, f*f dominated by a few near-coincident spike products so that linf is ~1.2x the L2-per-unit-mass scale. Its lever is not flattening (p-norm with p up to 2048 left the peak sharp) but more resolution + higher p + restarts, which gave +4.5e-4 at N=6400. It should keep gaining ~1e-4 per experiment but is unlikely to reach 0.8582 without a genuine peak-lowering mechanism.
refuted_if: A further N=12800 / higher-p push of p0097 gains less than 5e-5, or the sparse line exceeds 0.858176.
